note: [agent-bulk] numucc_em, 28 showers, 5 in scope (14007, 28036, 60050, 64054, 50049 -- all pdg 11). Verdict shower 14007 (kine_charge 616.1, 5 seg) -- the first pdg-11 entry of in_scope and the highest-charge object in the event; no non-EM object outranks it. The 23 skipped showers are sub-20 MeV, but many of them ARE the subject of this finding, so I read them off the segment table rather than treating them as unlooked-at. Vertex judged off the vtx-* sweep at 126.8 cm half-span (r95 101.4, under the 150 cm trigger, no vtxz-*). It is good: the star sits at the apex of a clean two-armed V -- the 88.8 cm pdg-13 track 14001 (unowned, correctly grey) on one arm and the shower on the other, and the shower start X sits 3.7 cm from it. UNDER-CLUSTERED. 14007's own skeleton stops at 41.6 cm from the vertex (members 14007, 14073, 14010, 14011, 14008; cmp_div 0.0-33.9 cm from the start, 0.0-11.5 deg). Beyond that, along the shower's OWN axis (vertex -> member centroid = (-0.034,0.723,0.690)), there is a train of about 25 segments at 7-25 deg running out to 102 cm, split among ~15 separate objects: 60050 (50.9 MeV), 28036 (58.4), 64054 (38.2), 50049 (35.5) and a dozen singleton sub-20 MeV showers (49048, 63053, 78068, 46045, 48047, 47046, 76066, 77067, 80070, 72062, 79069, 68058). For a 616 MeV EM shower that pattern reads as a shredded tail, not as fifteen particles. The corroboration the brief asks for is on the acceptance plot: 49048 is a CIRCLE at 25.8 cm / 7.4 deg, well inside the 15 deg pass-1 gate, and 50049 is a circle at 41.7 cm / 15.0 deg sitting exactly ON it -- two non-members inside or on the gate. MARKS, IN, and they differ in strength (correction 7): 50049 IN is the strong one -- 3.5 cm, 7 fitted points, the seed of its own 35.5 MeV shower, 5.5 cm from 14007's skeleton and on the gate line. 49048 IN is the weak one and the one I would let the owner reverse -- it sits deepest inside the cone (6.5 deg to the own-axis, 4.5 cm gap) but it is a 0.2 cm two-point stub carrying no charge, so it changes the energy by nothing. NOT MARKED but named: 60050 (4.4 cm / 9 points, 50.9 MeV, gap 6.1 cm) is as close as those two but sits at 24.4 deg to the own axis, outside the 15 deg gate, so a mark on it would over-claim; and 28036 (7.9 cm / 14 points, 58.4 MeV, 10.2 deg) is on-axis but 13.6 cm off the skeleton. Correction 11/16 caveat, stated because it is the main risk here: none of this charge is grey -- every piece is owned by a neighbouring shower or is the seed of its own sub-20 MeV shower, which is exactly the unsafe basis the corrections warn about. I ran the triple-check on 14007 and all three agree (nseg 5 == owner-grouped 5 == cmp_div 5), so the display is not lying about ownership and these really are non-members; my claim is the physics one, that the reconstruction should have merged them, not that the table is wrong. PI0: the reco has NO pi0 group (every pio_id is -1), so the [14007, 28036] pair in the pio-* frames is the capture's automatic top-two slotting (correction 3) and not the reconstruction's pairing. Priced, it fails: the display gives m = 62.9 MeV on the axis convention (theta 19.1 deg) and 29.5 MeV on the vertex convention (theta 8.9 deg), and for E1 616.1 / E2 58.4 the opening angle needed for 135 MeV is 41.7 deg. So 28036 cannot be the partner gamma of 14007, which removes the innocent explanation for a second EM object sitting 10 deg off the leading shower's axis and supports the under-clustering reading. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID.
